title: Civic Contact Institute — Seeing, Concluding, and Knowing What the Law Actually Says
label: EDUCATIONAL — reasoning practice, not legal advice. Law varies by jurisdiction and changes over time.

modules.title: Observation
modules.goal: Say only what was seen, heard or recorded.
modules.drill: Rewrite ten sentences so each keeps only what a camera could capture.

modules.title: Inference
modules.goal: Name the observations every conclusion rests on; list at least one other explanation.
modules.drill: For each inference, write two rival explanations that fit the same observations.

modules.title: Legal standards are defined by law, not by feeling
modules.goal: Recognise that terms such as reasonable suspicion and probable cause are legal standards whose meaning depends on the jurisdiction's law and courts.
modules.drill: Given a scenario, state which jurisdiction's law would apply and what source you would need to read. Do not guess the answer.

modules.title: Jurisdiction and date
modules.goal: Every legal statement names a place and an as-of date.
modules.drill: Mark each statement in a news story as jurisdiction-specific, date-specific, both, or neither.

modules.title: Lawful escalation
modules.goal: Safety first; document; ask plain questions; use lawful review channels afterwards; consult licensed counsel for what the law requires.
modules.drill: Order the escalation steps and explain why physical resistance is never on the list.

source_policy.rule: No lesson may state what an Earth law requires or permits unless a legal_source_registry row with world_layer EARTH, jurisdiction, official_source_uri, effective_from and evidence_status VERIFIED_OFFICIAL_TEXT is attached.
source_policy.current_backend_state: legal_source_registry holds no rows for these standards as of 2026-09-24; M3 therefore teaches how to find the source, not what it says.
